_comment: PERFORMANCE suite: the ingestion throughput of the Kafka stream source over JSON -- the rows a stream publisher writes to its files per second, before a trigger makes them a manifest -- over 10000000 messages on <prefix>.employees (one partition), each an employees row as JSON, ~130 bytes, validated against a typed JSON Schema, written before the stream starts so it reads a backlog. The publisher (functions/perf_kafka.py::kafka_json) has the CDC performance publishers' buffer and trigger. STAGES: (1) domains -- create the redpanda domain and install the employees model, which creates its topics; (2) actions -- 40 passes of `modify-data --entity employees --size 2500`, 250000 messages each (in passes: one load builds every table of the model, ~12 rows for each employee sent); (3) collections; (4) functions -- register the publisher, which STARTS it; (5) actions -- scripts/cdc_throughput.py (the stream ledger it reads is every stream source's) reads the stream worker's log until its files hold 10000000 rows or 10m has passed, and says in the step's note the end-to-end figure -- rows, files, MB, seconds from the plugin's run() to the last file, rows/s -- and the read figure -- rows the source yielded, the seconds the plugin waited on it for them, rows/s (PARTIAL when short; the step still passes); (6) monitor. Generated by gen_suites.py. Run one at a time: `tdd xp one-shot --suite performance/kafka_json`.
